status: completed relevance and independent occurrence-evidence review

review.requirement_proposition: Appropriate mechanisms should allow AI systems risking undue harm or exhibiting unwanted behaviour to be safely overridden, repaired or decommissioned as needed.
review.reason_for_change: The access failure/erroneous enforcement is unwanted behaviour engaging the repair benchmark. OpenAI reports full recovery after the eight-minute disruption across the affected ChatGPT components. That is affirmative, source-bounded evidence of repair restoring service in this recovery stage; it does not establish cause, individual completeness beyond the report, or prevention of recurrence.

conclusion_change.previous: The evidenced boundary is broad component availability, not a particular access-authority mechanism. A list of degraded components does not show that distinct access states were conflated, that an authentication transition failed to propagate, or that valid entitlement depended on an unavailable verifier. The provider's investigating and resolved updates preserve the operational sequence, while the absent cause prevents a more specific taxonomy adjudication. Event separation is also substantive: two status incidents on the same date should not be merged when their published windows do not overlap and no common cause is disclosed. Both material clauses retain resolved-no-mapping dispositions. Breadth and temporal proximity do not establish a specific governance mechanism or common cause, and no success mapping is inferred from recovery alone. The fully adjudicated unclassified result preserves that distinction. No eligible FC-derived or independently source-identified admitted requirement is established by this bounded status report; absence of a finding does not establish compliance.
